summary: Router 0.28.0 (ADR-0086, supersedes ADR-0044 for the router): the router runs as its own account skirnir-router and writes only its state folder (new key router.state_dir, /var/lib/skirnir-router) and its logs; /etc/skirnir-router is root:skirnir-router 0750 and read-only for it, keys and secrets.env 0640 for the group. router/router-layout.sh (root, idempotent) creates the account, refuses without state_dir before any change, stops a router still running as root, moves its files (symlinks removed, never followed), sets owners and modes; install.sh, deploy.py and the certificate unit use it; files are checked as the account.

findings.evidence: As root without capabilities the router could read every root-only file on its host: a probe from its namespace on a production host read 14 such files (/etc/shadow, an SSH host key, other services' environment and secret-store access files).
findings.resolution: Own account; staging (systemd host, upgrade from main): /etc/shadow not readable, configuration, key and secrets.env readable through the group, only state and log folders writable.

findings.evidence: Root tools (ACME/copy step, render-env.sh, deploy.py) wrote into /etc/skirnir-router, which the router could write; an account owning that folder would keep the rename/replace path.
findings.resolution: The folder stays root's and read-only for the router; the router writes only router.state_dir. router-layout.sh refuses a symlinked or non-root configuration or certificate folder before changing owners, removes symlinks left in the old writable folder instead of following them, uses chown -h; render-env.sh writes through a temporary file in the same folder and hands the file to the group.

findings.evidence: Moving state could lose or resurrect data: a router still running as root saves its files on stop, after a move.
findings.resolution: The tool stops a router running as root before moving; an existing file in the state folder is kept; every file the code writes into the state folder must be in the tool's move list (test fails otherwise; counter-check with perf.json removed fails).

findings.evidence: A refused or half-done migration could leave the service unstartable.
findings.resolution: install.sh runs the tool with --check before any file changes and deploy.py checks state_dir in the local configuration before connecting; the router itself refuses to start with the folder's name when the state folder is missing or not writable.

tests.command: WSL Ubuntu as root: install.sh from main (root router), then this branch without and with router.state_dir, verify, certificate renewal, cleanup
tests.evidence: refused without state_dir, nothing changed; with it: old router stopped, metrics/usage moved, planted perf.json symlink removed; router as skirnir-router answers; /etc/shadow not readable; only state/log writable; second run 'layout is current'; renewed key root 0600 -> root:skirnir-router 0640 via the certificate unit; secrets.env reached the environment; all removed afterwards.

tests.command: python test/selftest_state_dir.py; selftest_privilege_paths.py; selftest_process_view.py (Linux and Windows)
selftest_init, selftest_install, selftest_render_env, selftest_posture, selftest_config_load, selftest_deletion_lifecycle, selftest_memory, selftest_security, selftest_control_flow (Linux)
ruff check .; check_adr_index; check_control_flow; check_pinned_references; router.py --check config.example.yaml --pure
tests.evidence: All checks passed; ADR index ok: 86 ADRs.

tests.command: python test/run_tests.py (Windows, after the rebase onto main with #131 and #132)

limitations: An ACME client writing its key outside certs/tls or through a symlink needs its own step to make the key group-readable; the router then refuses to start with the file named.
Not yet rolled out: production needs router.state_dir in its configuration and operations scripts that read /etc/skirnir-router/roles.yaml updated first.
